title: Arranging the number transcribed as 'B'libao'
summary: Gil explains why he wanted the melody played in a free, crying way over a fixed dance beat.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: May we come back to a particular arrangement of yours and that is (Still Bowl?) 'B'libao'. Would you talk about that a little bit because I don't know how else to describe it. I sort of said it's the kind of lethargic kind of interpretation and I'm wondering just what you had in mind?
Let's see now, where did I hear that number?
Oh it was a popular number, very popular.
Yes. It was a very, you know......
Yes. I don't remember who did it.

I didn't know it was a popular number. I forget where I heard it but the opening, I just had an idea that I wanted to hear that in a free kind of crying way you know. When they played, just the melody and I had the rhythm started out playing just a regular fixed beat you know, a pattern a dance pattern. And I just conducted the band like note for note, melody right? Each melody, each note.
Like you're in a big canyon or something open where you hear these tremendous reverberations, you know. That kind of sound. That was the part I had in mind for that.
